title: Google Sheets AI assistant for rows, ranges and reports
h1: a google sheets bot with a clear range to work in
description: Connect Google Sheets to Metal for row checks, table updates and charts. Copy focused routines that name their input range and write boundary.
answer: **find the stock that needs ordering before someone sells the last unit.** connect google sheets to a Metal bot, choose your ai and name the file, tab and cells. it can read rows, update values and make charts. get the first report in chat. when you want edits, add an ask-first instruction; cell changes do not automatically wait for approval.

review.by: lead agent: read against seo/facts, automated gate, independent fact-check pass

og_line: name the tab. bound the change.

app.name: Google Sheets
app.intro:
**tell the bot where headers end and formulas live.**

these actions find the right table and read its structure. they also let the bot update only the cells you intend.

highlight.use: find the tracker by title before touching a similarly named file
read the workbook structure and find the inventory tab
confirm the current tab names rather than guessing
find the row for a particular order reference
inspect the table columns before preparing new entries
write agreed values to a named destination range
add new records after existing entries instead of overwriting them
make a chart from the range you selected

app.setup:
**give the bot the tab and the actions it needs.**

in **connected apps**, sign in to google sheets and allow your spreadsheet bot to use it. google receives the sign-in. paste the spreadsheet reference into chat and name the tab.

for controlled updates, allow only the actions the job needs. don't grant the entire catalog.

routines_intro: **the bot needs column meanings, not just a file link.** say what counts as an exception and where changes may go. each message below names the result you should get.

routines.name: stock exceptions
routines.message: each monday at 9, read the inventory tab in my stock sheet. compare available units with each row's reorder level. list items below that level here, with row numbers. leave values and row order alone. if none are below it, say so in one line.
routines.output: a list of stock exceptions with their row numbers

routines.name: intake rows
routines.message: every weekday at 5, read new request files added today to the intake requests project folder. compare them with the intake sheet to skip existing requests. prepare new rows using the sheet's column names. show the rows here and wait for me to approve the append. append only the rows i choose. never overwrite existing requests or guess missing details.
routines.output: new rows for your review, then an append only after your yes

routines.name: weekly chart check
routines.message: every friday at 2, read the weekly totals table in my sales sheet. report its covered dates and any empty weeks. propose a chart from only that table. wait for me to choose it before creating it. leave the source values alone.
routines.output: a date coverage check and a chart to approve

asks:
**keep cell changes tied to the range you chose.** updates, sorting and charts do not automatically wait for an approval card. put "ask me before you change anything" in the editing job.

leave find and replace off a reading bot's exact action list. dusk counts it as a read even though it changes cells. some lookup-like actions count as writes. choose actions by what they do, rather than how their names sound.
cannot: **a reading bot needs an exact action list here.** updates, appends and formatting need writes. find and replace is the exception: dusk counts it as a read, so leave it off.
**"clean this up" doesn't name a safe range.** identify the tab, headers and cells to leave alone. read the proposed edits first.
**a closed local app misses the monday check.** a run less than 12 hours late runs once on return. older runs skip.

sections.md:
**tell the bot whether that blank means missing stock or none left.** name the columns with formulas too. ask for the source range beside each finding so you can open the row that needs attention.

working from a file dropped in chat? see [excel files](/integrations/excel). that is a different route from a connected spreadsheet.

sections.h: start the chart with the right transactions
sections.md:
**a missing transaction stays missing in a beautiful chart.** if the question starts with billing records, read [stripe](/integrations/stripe) before planning the update.

connect [google drive](/integrations/google-drive) separately for other source files. say which source wins when figures disagree.

faq.q: can claude or chatgpt update my google sheet?
faq.a: **yes, through a bot using your chosen ai.** it needs the connected account, permission for that write and a clear destination range.

faq.q: does it ask before changing a cell?
faq.a: **not automatically.** cell edits sit outside the send approval rule. include the ask-first line and keep the allowed actions narrow.

faq.q: can it just tell me which rows look wrong?
faq.a: **yes. keep the result in chat.** ask for row numbers and reasons, and tell it to leave source values alone.
